_provenance: Reference comparison values, approximate from published literature — NOT measured by this benchmark suite, and not verified against specific papers (no citations were preserved). The former 'mercury_agent' row (0.85/0.80) had no generator or measurement behind it and was removed in the fabrication audit; measured Mercury results live in mercury_benchmark_results.json.
description: Peer comparison baseline results for unsupervised anomaly detection

methodology.evaluation: nominal: ROC-AUC and F1 on a held-out test set; the values below were not produced by running that protocol here
methodology.note: All methods are unsupervised anomaly detectors, not supervised classifiers

strengths: No training phase in novelty mode

honest_assessment.summary: Mercury-Agent's ensemble detector (combining statistical, ML, and symbolic methods) is competitive with established unsupervised anomaly detectors like IsolationForest and LOF. Its primary advantage is interpretability through neuro-symbolic fusion, not raw detection performance.
when_to_use_mercury: When interpretability of anomaly decisions is required
When dealing with diverse data types requiring adaptive profiling
When confidence calibration and uncertainty quantification matter
when_to_use_alternatives: When speed is critical and interpretability is not needed (use IsolationForest)
When labeled anomaly data is available (use supervised classifiers)
When memory is constrained (use simpler methods)
